provider: Notion (free plan) - file blocks & Files property

free_tier.stated: No total storage cap: 'Unlimited file uploads' on Free, but each file is capped at 5 MiB on Free (5 GiB on paid). Block limit is unlimited for a single-member Free workspace.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: no retention statement was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that retention is unlimited
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free; Notion serves via S3/presigned URLs on Cloudflare-fronted notion.com. File objects return 'An authenticated HTTP GET URL... valid for one hour', so links must be re-minted - no CDN you can pin a cache to without re-signing.

tooling: Official Notion API file-upload endpoints (single-part <=20 MiB, multi-part above with 5-20 MiB parts) + PlakarKorp/integration-notion and many notion-backup repos for bulk extraction; no rclone backend
chaining: Per-record unlimited: 5 MiB x unlimited files x unlimited blocks x unlimited free workspaces. A 20 TiB archive sharded into 5 MiB objects = ~4.2M objects - feasible at 600 req/min but ~5 days of continuous upload. This is the clearest 'unlimited count, tiny per-file cap' in the niche.
limits_note: 5 MiB per file on Free (hard, enforced by API); 20 MiB per single-part API upload; parts must be 5-20 MiB; 600 requests/min per workspace (avg 10/s) shared across all connections; only whitelisted MIME types (audio/document/image/video/CAD) - arbitrary binary is rejected

identity_cost.detail: derived from the record's prose, not from an identity field, and no signup was executed: p' in the niche. 5 MiB per file on Free (hard, enforced by API); 20 MiB per single-part API upload; parts must be 5-20 MiB; 600 requests/min per workspace (avg 10/s) shared across al

reliability_note: The MIME whitelist is the killer: no generic octet-stream blobs, so archival datasets must be packed as .zip/.7z/.tar which Notion does accept. Signed URLs expire in one hour, so serving 1 TB/day out of Notion means re-minting continuously.
